s: Today we're talking about traveling smart — getting through airports and train stations without stress.
I love traveling, but the airport part always makes me nervous.
Airports are full of announcements, long lines, and signs in a foreign language.
But a few key words make everything much easier.
Me too, until I learned some smart travel words.
Your itinerary is your detailed travel plan — the list of places you will visit, and when.
So like, my itinerary for next month is Rome, then Florence, then Venice?
I always print my itinerary before a big trip.
Actually, do you share your itinerary with your family?
I send my whole itinerary to my mom so she knows where I am.
Having a clear itinerary makes the trip feel real.
A good itinerary also saves money.
If your itinerary is planned in advance, you don't waste time deciding every morning.
That's when passengers get on the plane, right?
Boarding usually starts about forty minutes before the flight.
When they call your group, you show your ticket and walk onto the plane.
I always arrive early because I hate rushing during boarding.
Last time, the boarding was delayed and everyone stood in line forever.
I like to wait in my seat until the final boarding call.
The platform is the raised area next to the track where you get on the train.
You check the departure screen to find your platform number.
Like platform nine at a big station?
I once ran to the wrong platform and almost missed my train.
Always double-check the platform on the screen.
And when you change trains, that's a transfer.
A transfer is when you change from one vehicle to another during your trip.
For example, you might take a bus and then transfer to the metro.
In London I had a transfer from the train to the underground.
The signs for the transfer were really clear.
My last transfer gave me only ten minutes, and I had to run!
Speaking of seats — aisle or window?
The aisle is the long passage between the rows of seats.
An aisle seat means you can stand up easily.
I love the window, but on a long flight the aisle is better.
Last time I sat in the middle and climbed over two people every hour.
With an aisle seat you control your own space.
The flight attendant walks down the aisle with the drink cart, so you get served first too.
Now customs — the place at the airport where officers check your bags?
After you land in a new country, you go through customs.
Officers may ask what you bought abroad or look inside your bags.
The line at customs can be so long.
Once I waited at customs for almost an hour in New York.
Pro tip: have your passport ready before you reach customs.
That's a short stop between connecting flights.
A layover is the waiting time between your first flight and your next one.
A two-hour layover is perfect — enough time to relax, not enough to get bored.
My favorite layover was in Istanbul — five hours, so I explored the airport food court.
For a long layover, some airports let you leave and see the city.
Always check the rules before a long layover.
Before we move on, what's the difference between a layover and a connection?
A connection is the flight itself — the plane that takes you onward.
A layover is the waiting time between the two flights.
So the layover is the boring part, and the connection is the next flight.
And if your layover is long enough, you can sometimes turn it into a mini adventure in a new city.
Carry-on — the small bag you take onto the plane.
A carry-on is the bag you keep with you instead of checking it in.
I travel with only a carry-on, so I never wait at baggage claim.
Packing a small carry-on forces you to pack light.
My carry-on has everything for a whole week.
And a good carry-on fits in the overhead bin.
If your carry-on is too big, they make you check it.
A shuttle is a bus or small plane that travels regularly between two places.
The airport shuttle runs every twenty minutes between the airport and the city center.
Hotels often have a free shuttle too.
When I land late, I take the hotel shuttle instead of an expensive taxi.
Some shuttles need booking in advance, so check the shuttle schedule before your trip.
That's the next flight that continues your journey, right?
If you fly from Tehran to Paris with a stop in Istanbul, the Istanbul flight is your connection.
Miss your connection and you wait for the next one.
I once missed a connection because my first flight was late.
Now I always choose a connection with at least two hours between flights.
A tight connection is exciting only in movies.
A comfortable connection means coffee, not running.
Let's review all ten: itinerary, boarding, platform, transfer, aisle, customs, layover, carry-on, shuttle, connection.
I'll describe a situation, and you name the word.
You're at the airport and they call your group to get on the plane.
You change from a bus to a train downtown.
The detailed plan of your whole trip.
The small bag you keep with you on the plane.
Try using all ten words this week — plan your itinerary, arrive early for boarding, and always give yourself a comfortable connection.
